feedback_request.compare_against: Iteration 3 (mass 0.8, y = 0.07, wheel_track 0.12, same spread and footprint). Oval progress 0.1175 is the target to beat.

intent: Restore the iteration 3 geometry (y = 0.07, wheel_track 0.12, 16 mm sensors, 0.16 m spread) and test one oval lever by changing mass from 0.8 to 0.6 kg. Integrator: keep kp 3.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.2, base_speed 2.0, last_direction, and the 25-times-x weights (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), with no gain change. Expected result: oval progress above 0.1175 and max_error near or below 0.06, with s-bend progress near 0.165 and s-bend steering_oscillation at or below 0.15. If s-bend oscillation exceeds 0.15, restore mass 0.8 and test wheel_track 0.11 at y = 0.07 as the next single change.
learning: Evidence summary: y = 0.06 dropped s-bend progress to 0.04, so the forward lead is required for the s-bend (y = 0.04 and y = 0.06 both gave 0.04). Narrowing the track to 0.10 raised s-bend oscillation to 0.164 without moving oval progress. Oval progress has been 0.115 to 0.1175 in every race, so mass is the first oval lever to test. Hypothesis A: lower mass gives quicker turn response and lifts oval progress above 0.1175. Hypothesis B: lower mass pushes s-bend oscillation above 0.15 and the slalom gains line losses, so mass 0.8 should be restored.
rationale: Iteration 5 (wheel_track 0.12, y = 0.06) scored 36.76, the worst result since iteration 1. Its s-bend progress fell from 0.165 at y = 0.07 to 0.04, the same as the y = 0.04 baseline, so the forward lead is what carries the s-bend gain. Slalom still lost the line once per run. The Integrator's rule applies: at y = 0.06 the s-bend progress is below 0.12, so the lead returns to y = 0.07 at wheel_track 0.12. That is the iteration 3 design, which scored 54.90 with s-bend progress 0.165, s-bend steering_oscillation 0.144 (under the 0.15 limit), and oval steering_oscillation 0.074. Iteration 4 (wheel_track 0.10) scored 56.50, but its s-bend oscillation rose to 0.164, so narrowing the track is over-responding. Oval progress has been flat at 0.1175 across every test of track width and lead, so turn authority and lead are not the oval lever. The Integrator's rule for this case is to test one oval lever, mass, while the s-bend oscillation is at or below 0.15. The iteration 3 design meets that condition (0.144), so I restore y = 0.07 and wheel_track 0.12 and change only mass, from 0.8 to 0.6 kg. Lower mass lowers yaw inertia (mass times (body_length squared plus body_width squared) over 12), so the robot should respond more quickly on the oval. Sensor footprint (16 mm), spread (x = -0.08 to 0.08), body, wheel radius and the 25-per-metre weights are unchanged, so this race isolates the mass change against iteration 3. Expected result: oval progress rises above 0.1175, and s-bend progress stays near 0.165. The risk is that the quicker turn response pushes s-bend steering_oscillation above 0.15, which would mean mass 0.8 should be restored.
